Since \(x_k=\frac{C}{k(k+1)}\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^n x_k=N\), we get
\[
C\left(1-\frac{1}{n+1}\right)=N \implies C=\frac{N(n+1)}{n}.
\]
The smallest part is the last part:
\[
x_n=\frac{C}{n(n+1)}=\frac{N}{n^2}.
\]
Given \(x_n=\frac{1}{400}N\),
\[
\frac{N}{n^2}=\frac{N}{400}\implies n^2=400\implies n=20.
\]
\[
\boxed{20}
\]
